evidence.claim: Bangladesh called for immediate cessation of hostilities in Ukraine, urged all parties to respect the UN Charter, and asked them to resume diplomacy and dialogue to settle disputes peacefully.
evidence.title: 2022_Statement_DPR_Ukraine Crisis.
evidence.publisher: Permanent Mission of Bangladesh to the United Nations, New York
evidence.excerpt: Bangladesh called for immediate cessation of hostilities in Ukraine, urged all parties to respect the UN Charter, and asked them to resume diplomacy and dialogue to settle disputes peacefully.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary contemporaneous UN mission statement with explicit Bangladesh position and date.
evidence.period_fit: directly within 2022 and tied to the Ukraine war response
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to Bangladesh’s UN delegation under the Hasina government; it reflects state policy, not battlefield command.
contrary_evidence: The statement is diplomatic and not a test of military restraint in a live war.
It does not show a Hasina-only decision distinct from the foreign ministry.

evidence.claim: Bangladesh voted for the UN resolution on Ukraine’s territorial integrity and said it did so because the UN Charter’s principles on sovereignty, territorial integrity, and peaceful settlement must apply universally.
evidence.title: Bangladesh votes for UN resolution against Russia
evidence.excerpt: Bangladesh voted for the UN resolution on Ukraine’s territorial integrity and said it did so because the UN Charter’s principles on sovereignty, territorial integrity, and peaceful settlement must apply universally.
evidence.source_locator: news report quoting the foreign ministry statement
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous reporting quoting an official government explanation for the vote.
evidence.period_fit: directly in 2022 and directly tied to Bangladesh’s UN vote on the war
evidence.ruler_attribution: State policy under Hasina’s government; the vote is attributable to the government even if not personally signed by Hasina.
contrary_evidence: This is a diplomatic vote, not evidence of operational coercive restraint.
It came after earlier abstentions, so the posture was mixed rather than uniformly hard-line.

evidence.claim: Bangladesh abstained on the UNGA resolution about Russian reparations for Ukraine, showing continued caution even after later 2022 pro-Ukraine voting.
evidence.title: Bangladesh abstains from UN vote against Russia
evidence.excerpt: Bangladesh abstained on the UNGA resolution about Russian reparations for Ukraine, showing continued caution even after later 2022 pro-Ukraine voting.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraphs on the UN vote and Bangladesh’s abstention
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous reporting, but the article is summary-level and does not add ruler-specific reasoning beyond the vote itself.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Bangladesh’s government position under Hasina, not to a battlefield command decision.
contrary_evidence: The abstention may reflect diplomatic hedging rather than principled restraint.
It cuts against a simple narrative of consistently aligning with anti-aggression votes.

evidence.claim: Bangladesh said it had taken multi-pronged diplomatic efforts bilaterally and multilaterally to facilitate the safe, voluntary, and sustainable return of Rohingya refugees and warned the crisis could become a regional security crisis.
evidence.title: 2022_Statement_DPR_Situation of Rohingya Muslims in Myanmar
evidence.publisher: Permanent Mission of Bangladesh to the United Nations, New York
evidence.excerpt: Bangladesh said it had taken multi-pronged diplomatic efforts bilaterally and multilaterally to facilitate the safe, voluntary, and sustainable return of Rohingya refugees and warned the crisis could become a regional security crisis.
evidence.source_locator: statement body, especially the paragraphs on diplomatic efforts and regional security risk
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary UN mission statement with clear dated policy language and explicit diplomatic aims.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State diplomacy under Hasina’s government; attributable to the government, though not a personal military order.
contrary_evidence: Again, this is a process statement, not proof of successful repatriation.
It reflects humanitarian/diplomatic handling more than a direct aggression decision.

evidence.claim: Modi said India and Bangladesh signed a Kushiyara river water-sharing agreement and discussed flood mitigation and cooperation against terrorism and radicalism during Hasina’s visit.
evidence.title: English Translation of Press Statement by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi during the visit of Prime Minister of Bangladesh to India
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
evidence.excerpt: Modi said India and Bangladesh signed a Kushiyara river water-sharing agreement and discussed flood mitigation and cooperation against terrorism and radicalism during Hasina’s visit.
evidence.source_locator: press statement paragraphs on the Kushiyara agreement, flood mitigation, and anti-terror cooperation
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official government press statement with specific signed agreement and meeting themes.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to Hasina’s state visit and bilateral diplomacy, though the wording is from the Indian side.
contrary_evidence: This is the Indian prime minister’s statement, so it is an external corroboration rather than a Bangladesh-authored record.
It does not directly evaluate Hasina’s peace conduct beyond the diplomatic agenda.

evidence.claim: India and Bangladesh signed the Kushiyara water-sharing MoU on 6 September 2022, creating a joint monitoring team and formalizing a cooperative border-river arrangement.
evidence.title: Cabinet approves Memorandum of Understanding between India and Bangladesh on withdrawal of upto 153 cusecs of water each by India and Bangladesh from common border river Kushiyara
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
evidence.excerpt: India and Bangladesh signed the Kushiyara water-sharing MoU on 6 September 2022, creating a joint monitoring team and formalizing a cooperative border-river arrangement.
evidence.source_locator: body text describing the signature date and monitoring mechanism
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specific treaty-like bilateral arrangement in an official government release with a concrete implementation mechanism.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Part of Hasina’s external diplomacy because the MoU was signed during her state visit, though the document itself is intergovernmental.
contrary_evidence: Water-sharing is a cooperation file, not a direct test of war/peace in a conflict.
It shows lawful management of shared resources rather than a broader strategic settlement.

evidence.claim: India and Bangladesh reiterated commitment to deepen cooperation on border and security issues, including border fencing, illegal crossing, insurgency, terrorism, organized crime, and smuggling.
evidence.title: 18th Meeting of the Joint Working Group (JWG) on Security and Border Management between India and Bangladesh held
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
evidence.excerpt: India and Bangladesh reiterated commitment to deepen cooperation on border and security issues, including border fencing, illegal crossing, insurgency, terrorism, organized crime, and smuggling.
evidence.source_locator: paragraphs describing the meeting agenda and bilateral commitments
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official government summary of a bilateral security-management meeting with concrete agenda items.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Hasina government’s border-management posture, though not a personal operational order.
contrary_evidence: Border-management cooperation is partly routine and not a special peace initiative.
This is bilateral security administration rather than conflict settlement.

evidence.claim: Across March and October 2022, Bangladesh’s Ukraine position combined an initial abstention justified in peace terms with a later vote explicitly supporting sovereignty and territorial integrity.
evidence.title: Bangladesh votes for UN resolution against Russia / Bangladesh abstains on related vote in March 2022
evidence.excerpt: Across March and October 2022, Bangladesh’s Ukraine position combined an initial abstention justified in peace terms with a later vote explicitly supporting sovereignty and territorial integrity.
evidence.source_locator: comparison of the March abstention reporting and the October affirmative vote reporting
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Two contemporaneous reporting strands together show the mixed but non-aggressive posture more clearly than either one alone.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government foreign policy under Hasina, with no evidence of any personal escalation order.
contrary_evidence: The mixture of abstention and support weakens any claim of fully consistent anti-aggression leadership.
It still does not amount to direct operational conflict conduct.

unresolved_gaps: No direct Hasina-specific 2022 decision on nuclear safety appointments, command-and-control, or emergency doctrine.
No independent audit of Rooppur safety performance or BAERA independence in the target year.
No direct Bangladesh-initiated interstate war, proxy war, or coercive military campaign in 2022.
Direct command-chain evidence for specific 2022 abuses remains thin.
Stronger direct evidence is still needed on institutional restraint, especially courts, election administration, and oversight bodies.
Household-level distribution and independent execution evidence are thinner than macro and program-announcement evidence.
Direct ruler causation for service delivery is thinner than outcome evidence.
Direct first-person evidence of correction, admission, or disclosure is still thin.
The plot-allocation/self-dealing allegations need stronger independent corroboration or final adjudication.
Independent audits of implementation quality and outcome progress are still limited compared with announced-program evidence.
Direct evidence that Hasina personally monitored, corrected, or replaced ineffective implementers is sparse.
